key_insight: Informative feature names help zero-shot Qwen-7B select features, especially for regression, but classical selectors generally outperform the tested 7B LLM/RL selectors.
engineering_relevance: Keep classical feature selectors as predictive-performance baselines, and test semantic LLM selection when compact, meaningfully named feature subsets matter.
method: Split 18 datasets into 10 for GRPO training, 2 for checkpoint validation, and 6 for held-out evaluation.
Compare five classical selectors, frozen Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.3-70B, and two GRPO-adapted Qwen2.5-7B models.
Evaluate ROC-AUC and R² separately, use dataset-wise ranks across tasks, and test feature-name sensitivity with matched subset sizes.
evidence_signal: Across five seeded evaluation partitions, informative names improved zero-shot Qwen-7B mean R² by 0.1964 versus anonymized names and 0.1606 versus shuffled names; corresponding ROC-AUC gains were smaller at 0.0159 and 0.0084.
watch_item: Semantic benefits were task- and dataset-dependent; results from six held-out datasets do not establish a general LLM advantage.
paper_title: When Do LLMs Help with Feature Selection? A Systematic Empirical Study
